title: Emerging Tech: WebAssembly (Wasm), eBPF Tetragon & Edge K3s
summary: Run sub-millisecond WebAssembly (WASI/SpinKube) serverless workloads alongside OCI containers, enforce kernel-level eBPF security with Cilium Tetragon, and operate K3s edge fleets.
learningObjectives: Deploy WebAssembly (Wasm) workloads on Kubernetes using RuntimeClass `wasmtime-spin`.
Enforce kernel-level eBPF process and network policies using Cilium Tetragon `TracingPolicy`.
Operate lightweight, low-footprint K3s/KubeEdge workloads for disconnected retail and IoT edge sites.

curriculumModules.title: WebAssembly on Kubernetes (SpinKube, containerd-shim-wasm & RuntimeClass)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: WebAssembly (Wasm) modules cold-start in under 1 millisecond with a memory footprint measured in kilobytes. containerd-shim-wasm allows kubelet to schedule Wasm workloads natively via Kubernetes `RuntimeClass`.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use `runtimeClassName: wasmtime-spin` for bursty, scale-to-zero edge and serverless HTTP workloads while keeping stateful databases in standard OCI containers.

curriculumModules.title: eBPF Kernel Security Enforcement with Cilium Tetragon
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Unlike user-space or asynchronous syscall monitors, Cilium Tetragon uses eBPF in-kernel LSM/kprobe hooks to block unauthorized binary execution or file access synchronously before the syscall completes.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy Tetragon `TracingPolicy` resources to prevent container breakout attempts and block unexpected outbound raw socket connections in kernel space.

labs.title: Deploying Sub-Millisecond WebAssembly Workloads with RuntimeClass
labs.scenario: Deploy a high-density serverless WebAssembly microservice (`wasm-edge-fn`) in `production` and configure its Pod template to use `runtimeClassName: wasmtime-spin`.
labs.productionContext: Kubernetes `RuntimeClass` routes Wasm pods to the `containerd-shim-spin` runtime on worker nodes for sub-millisecond cold starts.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: wasm-edge-fn
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: wasm-edge-fn
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: wasm-edge-fn
    spec:
      runtimeClassName: wasmtime-spin
      containers:
        - name: wasm-fn
          image: ghcr.io/spinkube/wasm-api:v1.0.0
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl get deploy wasm-edge-fn -n production -o json` to verify `spec.template.spec.runtimeClassName` is `wasmtime-spin`.

labs.title: Enforcing eBPF Kernel TracingPolicy with Cilium Tetragon
labs.scenario: Configure an eBPF kernel security policy ConfigMap `tetragon-ebpf-policy` in the `security` namespace with `enforcement=SIGKILL` to block unauthorized binary execution inside containers.
labs.productionContext: Cilium Tetragon enforces security policies directly in the Linux kernel using eBPF, terminating malicious processes before they can exfiltrate data.
objectives: Audit runtime security status using `falco status`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tetragon-ebpf-policy
  namespace: security
data:
  enforcement: SIGKILL

steps.title: Verify Kernel Runtime Security Status
steps.instruction: Run `falco status` to verify kernel eBPF probes are active.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which Kubernetes resource field allows scheduling a WebAssembly (Wasm) Pod alongside standard Linux OCI containers on the same cluster?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Kubernetes `RuntimeClass` selects which CRI runtime handler (such as `runc`, `crun`, `kata`, or `wasmtime-spin`) kubelet and containerd use to run a Pod.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cilium Tetragon differ from user-space log-based intrusion detection tools?
options: It only runs on Windows XP
It uses eBPF in-kernel hooks to observe and synchronously block (`SIGKILL` / `Override`) policy violations directly inside the kernel before the system call completes
It emails log files once a week
It requires recompiling the Linux kernel from scratch on every pod restart
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Tetragon performs synchronous in-kernel enforcement via eBPF without suffering from user-space TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) race conditions.
